caption: The gates of Eamonn Medley's Two-Mile-Borris Transport Museum dressed up for our Vintage Coffee Morning, with our pair of wooden planters either side echoing the cohesive village planter scheme. Eamonn opened the gates for the day and the museum became the focal point of the fundraiser (May 2026)

The Bord na Móna LM 336 locomotive, a Hunslet-built 3-foot-gauge Wagonmaster diesel that spent its working life shifting peat on the bogs at Allenwood in Co. Kildare and Derrygreenagh in Co. Offaly, now sitting on its own stretch of reassembled track at the museum. Saved from the scrap pile and part of the museum's run of recent industrial heritage. From left: Eamonn Medley (museum owner), Seamus Graydon and Frank Kennedy (May 2026)

Inside the shed, with the 1962 Morris Oxford and the 1968 Morris Minor pulled out for visitors and a model Red Arrow hanging overhead. Eamonn has been building this collection since 2016 and it now runs to 18 vehicles from the 1930s to the 1970s, alongside a brilliant section of transport memorabilia. A real treasure to behold (May 2026)

The crew on the day the bed for the locomotive went down, lined up with the brooms and shovels on a freshly poured concrete pad with the wooden edging just bedded in. This same stretch is where the Bord na Móna LM 336 sits now. A brilliant turnout of local hands and the kind of voluntary effort that quietly builds a place like this up (2026)

The shed in full swing at our very first Vintage Coffee Morning in 2022, with families squeezed in around the tables, the Lions Club volunteers in their high-vis vests working the room, and the cars and a model Red Arrow looking down from overhead. A brilliant snapshot of the village turning out for the day (2022)

Another corner of the morning, looking back across the tables towards an old wooden trap and the vintage cars lined up either side. Daffodils on every table, vintage motoring posters on every wall, and a fantastic crowd in for tea and a chat. The kind of community event the museum was made for (2022)

Two Lions Club members working the ticket table during the morning, with the Lions vests and the Lions jacket front and centre. Thurles Lions Club organises the coffee morning every year and the proceeds, around €4,000 each time, all go back to local charities (2022)
Behind the counter at the tea station, with the Lions Club lads and ladies pouring and serving non-stop. Brilliant volunteer effort, and the engine room of any good coffee morning (2022)

A great candid of the lads in the middle of nudging a vintage car into position before the doors opened, with the whole crew leaning in and laughing. Half the fun of running a place like this is the morning of an event when everything is being shuffled around (2022)
